    import math
    
    # Function to determine the interval of T based on a single observation
    def interval_from_observation(t, c):
        if c == 'green':
            return (t % (Tg + Ty + Tr), (t - Tg) % (Tg + Ty + Tr))
        elif c == 'yellow':
            return ((t - Tg) % (Tg + Ty + Tr), (t - Tg - Ty) % (Tg + Ty + Tr))
        else:  # c == 'red'
            return ((t - Tg - Ty) % (Tg + Ty + Tr), (t - Tg - Ty - Tr) % (Tg + Ty + Tr))
    
    # Initial interval for T based on the first observation
    min_T, max_T = interval_from_observation(observations[0][0], observations[0][1])
    
    # Intersect intervals based on all observations
    for t, c in observations[1:]:
        new_min_T, new_max_T = interval_from_observation(t, c)
        min_T = max(min_T, new_min_T)
        max_T = min(max_T, new_max_T)
        if min_T > max_T:
            return 0.0  # No valid T found
    
    # Calculate the length of the valid interval for T
    valid_interval_length = max_T - min_T + 1
    
    # Determine the length of the period

    # Calculate the probability

        green_length = Tg
    elif cq == 'yellow':
        green_length = Ty
    else:  # cq == 'red'
        green_length = Tr
    
    probability = (valid_interval_length * green_length) / (period_length * valid_interval_length)
    
    return round(probability, 3)
